subject: dung beetle
title: This Dung Beetle Quit Eating Dung. Now It Beheads Millipedes

scenes.text: One dung beetle gave up dung. It hunts something fourteen times its size.
In the Peruvian rainforest, this beetle is just eight millimetres long. Its prey can be over ten centimetres.
Scientists trapped over a hundred thousand dung beetles. This species ignored every bait except live millipedes.
It grabs the millipede, wedges its toothed head between two body segments, and pries.
It keeps prying until the head comes off. If the millipede coils up, the beetle simply waits.
Then it carries the body away on its back. Not every dung beetle rolls dung.

description:
A dung beetle from the Peruvian rainforest, Deltochilum valgum, has switched from dung to hunting live millipedes up to about 14 times its length.
Researchers trapped more than 100,000 dung beetles over 11 months; this species came only to live millipedes, and it decapitates them by prying between body segments with its toothed head (Larsen et al., Biology Letters, 2009).
Would you have guessed a dung beetle could be a predator?
first_comment: It was over 60 times more likely to go for an injured millipede than a healthy one. Which bug would you never want to meet if you were tiny?
